basic_identification.full_title: Copper Strip for Electrical Purposes — Specification (Third Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering / Copper and Copper Alloys (approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements for copper strips used for electrical purposes, featuring drawn or rolled edges (either round or square), supplied in annealed (O), half-hard (HB), and hard (HD) tempers. It applies to flat copper products over 0.15 mm up to and including 6 mm in thickness, of any width, generally supplied in coils or flat/folded lengths. These strips are primarily utilized for electrical connections and windings in transformers, busbars, and related electrical machinery.

revision_history.edition: Third Revision (revised to modify the maximum strip thickness to 6 mm, delete legacy copper cathode references, make edgewise bending optional, adjust mechanical properties, incorporate temperature correction factors, introduce eddy current testing, and establish straightness tolerances)

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Copper Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all copper strips for electrical purposes must conform to IS 1897:2008 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified copper strips in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Exemption is granted solely for export-oriented shipments. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial copper strip conductors.

requirements.detail: Every coil or packaged bundle of copper strip must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard reference to verify compliance.

The strips must be manufactured from electrolytically or fire-refined copper, conforming to the chemical composition limits of grade Cu-ETP (Electrolytic Tough Pitch) or Cu-FRHC (Fire Refined High Conductivity) as specified in IS 191. Purity is typically verified at a minimum of 99.90 percent copper content.
Applies to flat copper products over 0.15 mm up to and including 6.0 mm in thickness. Standard dimensions and tolerances must satisfy the limits laid down in IS 3052.
Strips are supplied as requested by the purchaser in one of three designated tempers: a) O — Annealed (Soft); b) HB — Half-hard; c) HD — Hard.
The strip surface must be clean, bright, smooth, and completely free from harmful defects such as scratches, scale, pitting, or inclusions. Non-coiled strips must be flat and free from twists.

For strips over 12 mm wide in the annealed state, the material must withstand being bent flat on its edge through 180 degrees around a former of radius equal to half the width of the strip without showing cracks. This test is inapplicable to strips 1 mm thick or below.

Rods must ensure high electrical transport efficiency at 20°C:
- Annealed (O): Max resistivity = 0.01737 ohm mm²/m (Min conductivity = 99.25% IACS);
- Half-hard (HB) and Hard (HD): Max resistivity = 0.01777 ohm mm²/m (Min conductivity = 97.00% IACS).
Resistivity is measured per IS 3635, and eddy current probe testing is permitted by agreement.
Tolerances on straightness and edgewise curvature must be highly restricted: the strip must not deviate from a straight line by more than 3 mm over any 1,000 mm length.

Consignments of identical widths, thicknesses, and tempers are grouped into inspection lots of up to 2,000 kg. Visual and dimensional audits are conducted individually. Chemical analysis requires 1 sample per 2,000 kg lot, mechanical testing requires 1 sample per 500 kg lot, and resistivity is tested at 1 sample per bundle.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1897 : 2008 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing continuously cast, rolled, or drawn copper strips (over 0.15 mm up to 6.0 mm thick) used for electrical purposes—such as busbars, switchgears, panels, and windings inside transformers and rotating machinery. Under India's statutory Copper Products Quality Control Order (QCO), all copper strips supplied to the Indian market must conform to this standard and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). It regulates the chemical purity of the copper (conforming to ETP or FRHC grades with at least 99.90% purity) and classifies strips into annealed, half-hard, and hard tempers. The standard enforces strict limits on room-temperature mechanical properties (tensile strength and elongation), close-contact bending behavior (both transverse and longitudinal), straightness (maximum 3 mm deviation over a 1-meter length), nominal corner radii, and dry electrical resistivity (restricted to a maximum of 0.01737 to 0.01777 ohm mm²/m at 20°C to guarantee efficient power transmission).
